solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Disorderly, hungover husband leaves nick with half-cut male (12)

indicatorNotes.leaves: to leave is to depart, so the husband (H) walks out of HUNGOVER and the letters close up behind him
indicatorNotes.half-cut: cut in half, MALE keeps only one of its two halves, here the back end

blocks.note: to nick is to nab, i.e. arrest

annotation.surface: A drunk husband staggers out of the police station with an equally tipsy man.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Half-cut' is British slang for drunk, which suits the hungover husband, but here it simply trims MALE to its last two letters. 'Nick' is British slang for a police station, but it works as the verb 'arrest'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone ungovernable cannot be kept in order, which is what disorderly describes.

entries.clue: Tremulous at heart, groom left after meal (7)

indicatorNotes.at heart: the heart of anything is its centre, so only the central letter of the word is wanted

blocks.note: the middle (fifth) letter of the nine-letter TREMULOUS
to groom is to tidy, neaten

annotation.surface: A nervous bridegroom is abandoned once the wedding breakfast is over.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'groom' a bridegroom and 'left' his jilting; in fact 'groom' is the verb to tidy and 'left after meal' is the whole definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive phrase for the adjective: food nobody ate is what remains on the plate once the meal is over.

entries.clue: Chap concealing new note about revolutionary weapons (7)

indicatorNotes.concealing: to conceal is to hide inside, so GUY wraps round the other letters
indicatorNotes.revolutionary: a revolution is a turning round, so the word it touches, RE, is turned back to front

blocks.note: a guy is a chap; he goes round the rest
n. is the abbreviation for note

annotation.surface: A man hides guns for a revolutionary cause.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' looks like a noun for a rebel hiding arms; it is an adjective applied to 'about'. N for note is the dictionary abbreviation, not a musical note.
annotation.definitionFit: A collective sense: gunnery can mean heavy guns taken together, a force's weapons.

entries.clue: Second-hand vehicle covered by six promissory notes (9)

indicatorNotes.covered by: something covered has other things over it on both sides, so CAR is enclosed by VI and IOUS

blocks.note: IOUs are written promises to pay

annotation.surface: Someone pays for a used car with a handful of IOUs.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Second-hand vehicle' reads as a used car, but the hyphenated word is the definition on its own, in the sense of experienced through others.
annotation.definitionFit: A figurative sense: vicarious experience comes through someone else, so it is second-hand rather than lived directly.

entries.clue: Cadre beaten up and shot (5)

indicatorNotes.beaten up: something beaten up is knocked out of shape, so the letters of CADRE are knocked into a new order

annotation.surface: Members of a party cadre are assaulted and then shot.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shot' looks like gunfire in a violent surface; it is the verb of speed, as in 'shot past'.
annotation.definitionFit: A verb of speed: a car that shot past went very fast, so it raced.

entries.clue: Settle on Scottish island, coming home at last (7)

indicatorNotes.at last: at last means finally, so each of the two words before gives only its final letter

blocks.note: Arran is an island in the Firth of Clyde
last letters of comING and homE

annotation.surface: Someone decides to settle on a Scottish island, finally coming home.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Settle on' reads as making a home somewhere; 'Settle' alone is the definition, in the sense of fixing details, and 'on' puts ARRAN above the rest in this down clue.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of fixing details: to settle a date or a deal is to arrange it.

entries.clue: Starts to learn all about colour of milk (7)

indicatorNotes.Starts to: the start of a word is its first letter, so each of the next three words gives its opening letter

blocks.note: first letters of Learn, All, About

annotation.surface: A pupil begins learning about what colour milk really is.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is an adjectival phrase: lacteal means of or relating to milk, which is why 'of milk' swaps in for it.
annotation.definitionFit: A technical adjective from Latin lac, milk: lacteal describes anything relating to milk.

entries.clue: I for one desperately mourn real man (5,7)

indicatorNotes.desperately: acting desperately means acting wildly, so the letters are thrown into a frantic new order

annotation.surface: Someone speaking for themselves admits to grieving hard for a genuine man.
annotation.walkthrough: 'I for one' reads as a speaker volunteering an opinion; it is the letter I, which stands for one.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the letter I, standing for the number one, is one instance of the Roman system.

entries.clue: Vast abuse of cocaine (7)

indicatorNotes.abuse of: to abuse something is to misuse it and knock it about, so the letters of COCAINE are mistreated into a new order

annotation.surface: A news report on huge-scale cocaine misuse.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Abuse' belongs to drug talk in the surface; its job is to jumble the seven letters of COCAINE.
annotation.definitionFit: A figurative sense: oceanic means on the scale of an ocean, hence immense.

entries.clue: Onset of breathlessness after clown inhales Senior Service and pipe (7)

indicatorNotes.inhales: to inhale is to draw something inside yourself, so COCO takes RN into its middle
indicatorNotes.Onset of: the onset is the very beginning, so only the first letter is wanted
indicatorNotes.after: after means following, so B is placed at the end

blocks.note: Coco the Clown, a famous circus clown; RN goes inside him
the Royal Navy, nicknamed the Senior Service as the oldest British armed force

annotation.surface: A clown, puffing on a sailor's brand of cigarette and a pipe, starts to wheeze.
annotation.walkthrough: Senior Service was also a British cigarette brand, which is why 'inhales' fits so well; in the wordplay it is the Royal Navy.
annotation.definitionFit: A kind of pipe named for its material: a corncob pipe has its bowl carved from a dried corn cob.

entries.clue: Spooner’s take on his characteristic hobby (12)

indicatorNotes.Spooner’s take on: Rev William Spooner was famous for swapping the opening sounds of words, so his version of a phrase swaps its initial sounds

blocks.note: Spooner's trademark was word-botching; WORD takes the B of BOTCHING, and 'burd' is spelt BIRD
BOTCHING takes the W of WORD, and 'wotching' is spelt WATCHING

annotation.surface: A remark on the favourite pastime of the famously muddled Reverend Spooner.
annotation.walkthrough: The wordplay is never written out: Spooner's characteristic habit was word-botching, and swapping its initial sounds gives bird-watching.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: watching wild birds is a pastime many people take up, one hobby among many.

entries.clue: Insectivorous African gannets regularly breed (7)

indicatorNotes.regularly: something done regularly happens at even intervals, so every second letter is taken

blocks.note: the even letters of gANnEtS: A, N, T
to bear young is to breed

annotation.surface: A note on African seabirds that breed regularly, perhaps eating insects.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is an adjective phrase standing for an animal: the antbear, or aardvark, is an African insect-eater.
annotation.definitionFit: A description standing for the animal: the antbear, another name for the aardvark, is an African mammal that feeds on ants and termites.

entries.clue: Nursed a mercurial ballerina’s partner (7)

indicatorNotes.mercurial: mercurial means volatile and changeable, so the letters shift into a new order

annotation.surface: A temperamental ballerina's partner has been nursed through an injury.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mercurial' suggests a moody person, the partner perhaps; it signals that NURSED A is rearranged.
annotation.definitionFit: A description by role: a danseur is a male ballet dancer, the one who partners and lifts the ballerina.

entries.clue: Charlie is popular name in New York (5)

indicatorNotes.in: in means inside, so the letters before it are placed within New York's abbreviation

blocks.note: the usual abbreviation; it goes round the rest

annotation.surface: Charlie is the fashionable baby name in New York.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Charlie' looks like a name, but in British slang a charlie is a fool.
annotation.definitionFit: A British slang sense: calling someone a proper charlie means they are a fool, a silly person.

entries.clue: Fraternity member felt endlessly glum after rum (9)

indicatorNotes.endlessly: without its end, so FELT loses its last letter
indicatorNotes.after: after means following, so the other pieces come behind ODD

annotation.surface: A club member drinks rum and feels miserable without end.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rum' is the drink in the surface but the old British adjective for odd in the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A specific example: the Oddfellows are a British friendly society, a fraternal order, and each member is an Oddfellow.

entries.clue: Dirty dancing with dirty look (9)

blocks.note: disco is a style of dancing
to lour is to frown, a dirty look

annotation.surface: Suggestive dancing earns someone a disapproving glare.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dirty dancing' reads as the film; 'Dirty' alone is the definition, used as a verb, and the second 'dirty' belongs to 'dirty look'.
annotation.definitionFit: A verb sense: to dirty a surface is to stain it, changing its colour for the worse.

entries.clue: Profits from one’s times abroad (9)

indicatorNotes.abroad: abroad once meant widely scattered, so the letters are spread about

annotation.surface: Someone makes money from their years spent overseas.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Abroad' completes a travel picture, but here it means widely scattered.
annotation.definitionFit: A business sense: to monetise an asset is to turn it into a source of income, so to profit from it.

entries.clue: Not very musical group fronting Oscars (4,3)

indicatorNotes.fronting: to front something is to stand before it, so NONET goes in front of OO

blocks.note: O is Oscar in the NATO alphabet, so two of them

annotation.surface: A band playing at the Oscars is not very musical.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Oscars' suggests the film awards; it is the phonetic-alphabet word for O, doubled.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: 'none too pleased' means not very pleased, the phrase working as a mild negative.

entries.clue: Extra digit inhibiting Pole (2,5)

indicatorNotes.inhibiting: to inhibit is to hold something in check, so TOE holds SPAR inside it

blocks.note: a toe is a digit of the foot
a spar is a pole, as on a ship

annotation.surface: A Polish person has an extra finger that holds them back.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital P dresses 'Pole' as a nationality; it is a wooden pole.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: money or time to spare is more than needed, so extra.

entries.clue: Beer is forbidden on street (5)

indicatorNotes.on: in an across clue, one piece sitting on another follows it, so OUT comes after ST

annotation.surface: Drinking beer in the street is banned.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a local bylaw against street drinking, with 'is' as a plain link.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: stout is a dark, strong type of beer, such as Guinness.

entries.clue: Prepare champion for disappointment (7)

blocks.note: to set (a table, a trap) is to prepare it
to champion a cause is to back it

annotation.surface: Advice to get a champion ready for defeat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Champion' looks like a noun, the winner; it is the verb 'support'.
annotation.definitionFit: A near-synonym: a setback is a reverse in fortunes, the kind of event that disappoints.

entries.clue: Celebrity chef hosting current English actor (7)

indicatorNotes.hosting: a host has guests inside the house, so OLIVER holds I within it

blocks.note: Jamie Oliver, the British TV chef
I is the symbol for electric current

annotation.surface: A famous chef has a present-day English actor on his show.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like 'present-day', describing the actor; in physics I is the symbol for current.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Laurence Olivier, famed for Shakespeare on stage and screen, is the classic English actor.

entries.clue: Calls in during supper (5,2)

indicatorNotes.in: in means contained within, so the answer lies inside the words that follow

annotation.surface: Someone phones in the middle of dinner.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Calls in' reads as a phrasal verb, a visit; 'in' actually belongs to the wordplay, and 'during' is part of the text the answer is hidden in.
annotation.definitionFit: A British idiom: to ring someone up is to telephone them, to call them.

entries.clue: Quiet sound of sheep (not black) in fold (5)

indicatorNotes.not: 'not black' means without black, so B (black, as on pencil grades) is taken away

annotation.surface: A white sheep bleats softly in its pen.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fold' is a sheep pen in the surface, which is why 'in fold' reads naturally; the definition is fold as a crease.
annotation.definitionFit: A specific kind: a pleat is a fold pressed or stitched into fabric.

entries.clue: Duck — extremely succulent and fatty bird (7)

indicatorNotes.extremely: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only its first and last letters are taken

blocks.note: a duck is a score of nought in cricket, O
the first and last letters of SucculenT

annotation.surface: A menu note on duck: juicy, rich, a fatty bird.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Duck' wants to be the bird of the definition; it is O, a cricketer's score of nought, and the definition is the plain 'bird' at the end.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the ostrich, the largest flightless African runner, is one kind of bird.

entries.clue: Old salt shed light on hostility (7)

indicatorNotes.on: 'shed light on' ends with on, and in an across clue what comes on something follows it, so HATE comes after LIT

blocks.note: to have shed light is to have lit

annotation.surface: An old sailor has illuminated the hostility aboard ship.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Old salt' is a veteran sailor in the surface; the definition means a chemical salt with an old-fashioned name.
annotation.definitionFit: An obsolete chemical name: lithate is the former term for a urate, a salt of uric acid once called lithic acid.

entries.clue: Hand eggs one cracks to Head of Nutrition (7)

indicatorNotes.cracks: to crack something is to break into it, so I forces its way inside TO
indicatorNotes.Head of: the head is the top, so only the first letter is taken

blocks.note: used as it stands; I goes inside

annotation.surface: A nutrition chief is handed eggs, and someone breaks one.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hand' reads as the verb to pass; it is a noun, as in 'give them a big hand'.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: giving someone a big hand means applauding, and an ovation is enthusiastic applause.

entries.clue: Initially handed one shilling, penurious dons translated The Go-Between (6,6)

indicatorNotes.Initially: initially means at the start, so only the first letter of handed is taken
indicatorNotes.dons: to don is to put on clothing, so BROKE wears TR around it

blocks.note: s. was the abbreviation for the old British shilling coin
tr. = translated; it wraps round BROKE

annotation.surface: Poor university dons, paid a shilling each, translate L. P. Hartley's novel The Go-Between.
annotation.walkthrough: 'The Go-Between' is L. P. Hartley's novel, and 'dons' look like academics; here the definition is a go-between, and 'dons' means puts on. The shilling was a pre-decimal British coin.
annotation.definitionFit: A diplomatic idiom: an honest broker is a neutral party who mediates between two sides, exactly the role of a go-between.
